stagehand.title: STAGEHAND
lines: Stagehands. Wiry figures dressed head to toe in black, with gaffer tape round their wrists, headsets over their ears and faces you can never quite see, because the whole point of a stagehand is that you're not supposed to notice them.

They move the sets. They rig the lights. They clean up the blood between takes. They've been doing it so long that they've become part of the scenery: you can walk past fifty of them on the Backlot and never realise any of them were there until one of them's strangling you with a cable.
They take orders from the Floor Manager and nobody else. They don't talk. They whisper into their headsets, and somewhere, something whispers back.

Strengths: they're invisible until they aren't, they come from behind and they'll drop a light rig on your head from forty feet up. Weaknesses: they're crew, not cast. Get them on camera and they freeze like rabbits.
Kill one and another one quietly removes the body. You'll never see who.

the_extras.title: THE EXTRAS
lines: The Extras. Dozens of people in costumes from a dozen different sets: cowboys, astronauts, Victorian chimney sweeps, a nun, a man in a hot dog suit, all standing exactly where they were told to stand, with blank smiles and dead eyes.

They were contestants. All of them. Contestants who got to the Backlot and got cast as background, and never got a line, and never got a close-up, and never got to leave. They've been crossing the same street in the back of the same shot for years.

They get paid in sandwiches. They've been told that if they're very, very good, one day they'll be promoted to a speaking role. Nobody ever has been. One of them once said 'rhubarb', and they took him away.
Strengths: there are always more of them, they mob you in a crowd and they're in every bloody shot. Weaknesses: they don't have motivation. Literally. Nobody's told them what it is.
If one of them looks at you and mouths 'help', walk faster. That's how it starts.

boom_gremlin.title: BOOM GREMLIN
lines: Boom Gremlins. Spindly little green monkeys with huge ears, each one carrying a boom microphone three times longer than it is, which it holds directly over your head at all times.

They record everything. Every word, every grunt, every fart you let slip in a quiet moment. All of it, beamed straight up to the audience, who love it. Your best moments on the Backlot are mostly you swearing at a gremlin.

They giggle. They follow you. They'll dangle that boom into your shot just to ruin the take, then scurry off cackling. They're the most annoying creatures in the dungeon, and that's a dungeon with a Laugh Track in it.
Strengths: they're fast, they're in your face and they call the whole crew whenever you do something interesting. Weaknesses: they hate silence. Stand still and say nothing, and they get bored.
Smash a boom and the gremlin cries like a child who's dropped an ice cream. It's genuinely heartbreaking. You'll do it again.

floor_manager.title: FLOOR MANAGER
floor_manager.sub: Boss of Sound Stage 4. Places, please.
lines: The Floor Manager. A thin, harassed man with a clipboard, a headset, a lanyard full of passes and a stopwatch round his neck that he checks every three seconds, as if time personally owes him money.

He runs Sound Stage 4. He runs everyone on it. He tells the stagehands where to go, the extras where to stand and the contestants where to die. He's got a schedule, and you're in it, and you're running late.

He's been on the Backlot since the first episode. He has never had a day off. He has never had a break. He has never had a sandwich from craft services, because by the time he gets there, the Glutton's eaten them all.
Strengths: he summons stagehands, he drops scenery on you and he never stops shouting. Weaknesses: the schedule. Disrupt it and he falls apart.
Shout 'cut' at him. He'll stop dead, out of pure habit, for about two seconds. Use them.

the_stunt_double.title: THE STUNT DOUBLE
the_stunt_double.sub: Boss of the Western Set. Played your death.
lines: The Stunt Double. A broad, scarred man in a cowboy hat and a duster coat, with two revolvers, a face that's been broken in more places than it hasn't, and the uncanny feeling that you've seen him before. You have. In the mirror.

He does the dangerous bits. Every contestant who's been filmed on the Backlot has had a stunt double, and it's always him, wearing their face. He's played your death already. Seven times. Different angles. He's got it down to a fine art.

He's taken so many hits for so many people that he doesn't feel pain any more. He doesn't feel anything. He just waits on the Western Set for someone to say 'action', and then he does exactly what the script says.

Strengths: quick draw, dives, rolls and falls you'd break your neck doing, and he's been in every fight you're about to have. Weaknesses: he only knows the script. Do something stupid. He can't improvise.
Beat him at high noon and he'll take his hat off, look at you with your own face, and say 'nice'. Then he falls off the roof, perfectly, onto exactly the right spot.

makeup_witch.title: MAKEUP WITCH
makeup_witch.sub: Boss of the Makeup Trailers. Final look.
lines: The Makeup Witch. A tall woman in a smock covered in powder, with brushes stuck in her hair like pins in a cushion, a belt of a hundred lipsticks and a mirror that shows you who you're about to become.

She does faces. She can make you look like anyone. She can make you look younger, older, prettier, scarier, famous. And she does it permanently. Every face she's ever done is still on its owner. Some of those owners didn't want the faces.
She's the reason half the Extras look identical. She ran out of ideas in the eighties and just started doing the same face over and over. Nobody's dared complain.
Strengths: powder clouds that blind you, brushes thrown like darts and a face mask that slowly sets on your skin. Weaknesses: water. Makeup runs. So does she.
If you sit in her chair, she'll make you beautiful. Very beautiful. You'll never be able to stop smiling, ever again, because she's glued it on.

craft_services_glutton.title: CRAFT SERVICES GLUTTON
craft_services_glutton.sub: Boss of Catering. Ate the crew's lunch. And the crew.
lines: The Craft Services Glutton. A man so vast he fills the catering tent wall to wall, with a bib round his neck, crumbs in his beard, a cream horn in each fist and the sated, glazed expression of a python that's had a goat.

He was the caterer. He started eating the leftovers. Then the lunches. Then the crew. Then the extras, one sandwich at a time. Now he just sits in the tent and eats whatever comes in, and the Backlot has to send in more food, and more crew, and it never, ever ends.
He's not even hungry. He hasn't been hungry in decades. He just doesn't know how to stop. That's the Hollow Chef's work, if you believe in that sort of thing.
Strengths: he eats you, he rolls on you and he spits out half-chewed extras like cannonballs. Weaknesses: he can't move. At all. Stay out of reach.
When he dies, a hundred people climb out of him, covered in mayonnaise, blinking. Some of them are still holding sandwiches.

the_showrunner.title: THE SHOWRUNNER
the_showrunner.sub: Floor Boss of the Water Tank. Wants a different ending.
lines: The Showrunner. A man in a baseball cap and a gilet over an expensive shirt, sitting in a director's chair on a platform above the Water Tank, with a megaphone, a script and the dead-eyed confidence of someone who's never once been told his idea was shit.

He's in charge of every episode filmed on the Backlot, including yours. He's written your story. He's written your ending. And he doesn't like it. It's too soft. It needs a twist. It needs you dead in the tank, floating face down, with a slow zoom out.
He doesn't hate you. He just thinks it'd be better television. And he's not wrong. That's the worst part.
Strengths: he rewrites the scene mid-fight, he calls the whole crew down on you and he floods the tank. Weaknesses: he can't stand a bad take. Ruin his shot.
Wrap the bastard. Then walk off the set before he can call 'one more, from the top'.

mascot.title: MASCOT
mascot.sub: The Arena's team spirit. Inside a costume.
lines: Mascots. Giant foam costumes of animals that don't exist: a purple badger, a smiling sausage, a lion with a bow tie, a thing nobody can identify that might be a cheerful kidney. Inside each one is a contestant, sweating to death.
They're the Arena's hype men. They dance, they wave, they do backflips on the touchline and they beat the shit out of opposing players during the half-time interval for the crowd's entertainment.
The costumes don't come off. They were zipped in seasons ago, and the zips have rusted shut. You can hear them weeping in there between dances, very quietly, into the foam.
Strengths: they're padded like sofas, they dance-attack and the crowd goes wild every time they hit you. Weaknesses: they can't see properly. They can barely see at all.
Unzip one. It's horrible in there. But they'll thank you for it, with a long, wet, gasping breath.

big_foam_finger.title: BIG FOAM FINGER
big_foam_finger.sub: Boss of the Mascot Pen. Number one.
lines: Big Foam Finger. A giant foam hand, twelve feet tall, raised in the 'we're number one' position, with a face somewhere around the knuckle and a mascot's legs sticking out the bottom.

He runs the Mascot Pen. He's the most senior mascot in the Arena, and he got there by being the loudest and the pointiest. He believes he's number one. He's told so every match by forty thousand screaming fans.
He's not. He's never been number one. There's a Champion in this arena, and the Finger has never been allowed within a hundred yards of him. That eats at him.
Strengths: he pokes, he slams, he whips the mascots into a frenzy and he falls on you like a felled tree. Weaknesses: he's foam. He's top-heavy. Topple him.
Bend the finger back and he screams like you've broken a real one. You haven't. Probably.

ultra.title: ULTRA
ultra.sub: The Away End's finest. Here for the fight.
lines: Ultras. Shirtless, tattooed, scarf-wrapped hooligans in balaclavas, holding flares, banners and bits of the stadium they've ripped off, chanting songs whose lyrics are mostly swearing and the occasional threat against your mum.

They've been in the Away End since the first match. They've never seen a game. They're not here for the game. They're here to fight the away fans, and if there aren't any away fans, they'll fight you.
They have a code. It's mostly about scarves. Touch a scarf and you're dead. Wear the wrong scarf and you're very dead. Don't wear a scarf at all and you're a fucking tourist.
Strengths: they're never alone, they throw flares and they will not stop. Weaknesses: they'll follow anyone with a better chant.
Learn their songs. Sing them back. They'll go very quiet, and then they'll pick you up on their shoulders, and you'll be one of them for life. That's not a figure of speech.

the_capo.title: THE CAPO
the_capo.sub: Boss of the Ultras' End. Leads the chant.
lines: The Capo. A thick-necked man with a megaphone and his back permanently to the pitch, standing on a fence, leading the Ultras in song, with a face red from forty years of shouting and lungs like a pair of bagpipes.

He conducts the Away End like an orchestra of violence. He chooses the songs. He chooses the targets. He chooses when to charge. He has never watched a single minute of football, and he's furious about every result.
He needs a new anthem. The old one's got stale. The lads are bored. And a bored Ultra is a dangerous Ultra, mainly to himself.
Strengths: he rallies the Ultras, his chants buff the whole End and his megaphone blast knocks you flat. Weaknesses: the megaphone. Take it. He's nothing without it.
Give him a better song and he'll weep, and hug you, and smell of lager and smoke. Beat him and the End falls silent for the first time in history.

cheer_squad.title: CHEER SQUAD
lines: The Cheer Squad. Teams of cheerleaders in matching uniforms, with fixed grins and pom-poms full of razor blades, moving in perfect formation, never breaking step, never breaking smile.
They were contestants. They were chosen for their energy. Now they cheer for whoever's winning, and attack whoever's losing, in a perfectly choreographed routine they practise for nine hours a day.
Their smiles are fixed. The Makeup Witch did them. They haven't been able to stop smiling for years, and the muscles in their faces have gone hard as wood.
Strengths: they attack in formation, they throw each other at you and they never miss a beat. Weaknesses: break the formation and they don't know what to do. One out of step and they all fall.
Give me a D! Give me an E! Give me an A! Give me a D! What's that spell? You, if you're not careful.

head_cheerleader.title: HEAD CHEERLEADER
head_cheerleader.sub: Boss of the Cheer Pyramid. Top of the pyramid.
lines: The Head Cheerleader. A woman standing at the top of a human pyramid forty cheerleaders high, with a megaphone, a ponytail like a whip and a smile so wide it reaches her ears.

She's been at the top of the pyramid for six seasons. She has never come down. She eats up there. She sleeps up there. She has, God help us, gone to the toilet up there, and the squad at the bottom have simply had to live with it.
She's the Arena's queen. Encore loves her. She has more fans than anyone except the Champion. And she knows that the moment she comes down from that pyramid, somebody else goes up.
Strengths: she commands the squad, she leaps from the top of the pyramid and she dives down on you like a hawk. Weaknesses: the pyramid. Knock out the bottom row.
Topple her and the whole pyramid comes down in a screaming heap of pom-poms and limbs, and for one second, she'll look relieved.

the_ref.title: THE REF
the_ref.sub: Boss of the Officials' Room. Plays and referees.
lines: The Ref. A small, bald man in black and white stripes, with a whistle, a notebook and a set of red and yellow cards that are actually blades. He's not got a single friend in the whole stadium, and he's never wanted one.
He referees every match in the Arena. He's also, this season, your semi-final opponent. He sees no conflict of interest. He sees nothing at all, in fact, unless it's in his favour.
He can be bought. Everyone knows he can be bought. The Ultras buy him. The Champion's management buys him. He's been bought so many times that he's rich as fuck and has nothing to spend it on.
Strengths: yellow cards that slow you, red cards that send you off and a whistle that freezes you mid-swing. Weaknesses: he's tiny. Pick him up.
Beat him fair or beat him foul. He'll blow his whistle either way, and give you a yellow card on the way down.

the_champion.title: THE CHAMPION
the_champion.sub: Floor Boss of the Centre Circle. Last season's winner.
lines: The Champion. A huge man in a gleaming gold kit, every muscle oiled, a trophy in one hand and a belt on his waist, surrounded by spotlights, cameras and forty thousand screaming people who'd die for him. Some of them have.
He won last season. He's the last person to beat Ratings Week, and his prize was this: to be kept alive, here, in the Centre Circle, as the boss you have to beat. Forever. Until someone does.
He's tired. He's been the Champion for a year, and he's had nothing to do but win and win and win, and every time he wins, someone dies. He's started to hate the sound of applause.
Strengths: everything. He's fast, strong, armoured, the crowd roars every time he lands a hit and the crowd buffs him. Weaknesses: he doesn't want to be here.
As you walk out, he'll lean in and whisper: 'Don't win.' He means it. He's the only person in the Arena trying to help you.

laugher.title: LAUGHER
laugher.sub: The Laugh Track Factory's workforce. Ha. Ha. Ha.
lines: Laughers. Grey-faced people chained to desks in rows, laughing on cue. Forever. Their mouths have been laughing so long that their jaws have dislocated and hang open like broken drawers.
Every laugh you've ever heard on the Network is one of them. They're contestants, put to work in the Laugh Track Factory, laughing at jokes they can't hear, every time a light comes on. Ha. Ha. Ha.
Some of them have been laughing for thirty years. They've forgotten what funny is. They've forgotten what anything is. They just laugh, and laugh, and cry while they're laughing, and keep laughing.
Strengths: their laughter hurts. Literally. It's a sound weapon now. And they never stop. Weaknesses: they can't laugh without the cue light. Smash it.
Shut one down and it'll sigh. A long, empty sigh. The first sound it's made in years that wasn't a laugh.

the_laugh_track.title: THE LAUGH TRACK
the_laugh_track.sub: Boss of the Laugh Track Factory. Decides what's funny.
lines: The Laugh Track. A great grey machine of reels, tapes and speakers in the middle of the Factory, with a face made of an old reel-to-reel and a mouth that's a speaker cone, guffawing, chuckling, howling, tittering, all at once, constantly.
It decides what's funny. On the Network, if the Laugh Track laughs, it's comedy. If it doesn't, you're dead air. It has never laughed at anything genuinely funny in its life.
It's wired to every Laugher in the Factory. Every laugh they make feeds into it. It's built of a thousand people's mirth, and it's never once enjoyed any of it.
Strengths: sonic laughs that shatter your bones, cue lights that make the Laughers attack and it can laugh you to death. Weaknesses: tell it a genuinely good joke. It doesn't know what to do.
Get it on your side and every audience in the dungeon will laugh at you. That's useful. Horrible, but useful.

paparazzo.title: PAPARAZZO
lines: Paparazzi. Thin, sweaty men in anoraks with long-lens cameras, shoving each other out of the way, shouting your name, flashing so hard you can't see, getting so close you can smell what they had for lunch. It was a kebab.

They sell your worst moments to the Network. You on the toilet. You crying. You picking your nose behind a bin. You at the exact moment your face looks like a slapped arse. It's all money to them, and they have no shame whatsoever.
They were contestants. They found out that photographing people was safer than being photographed. They've been chasing stars down the corridors of the Green Room ever since.
Strengths: flash bursts that blind you, they swarm and they're impossible to get rid of. Weaknesses: break the camera and they're just sad men in anoraks.
Smash one's camera and he'll go on his knees in the corridor sobbing about his exclusive. Don't feel bad. He had a photo of you having a wank.

flash_mob.title: FLASH MOB
flash_mob.sub: Boss of the Paparazzi Pit. A thousand flashes.
lines: The Flash Mob. Fifty paparazzi so packed together that they've fused into one creature, a writhing ball of anoraks and long lenses, flashing constantly, shouting your name in fifty voices.
They are the Green Room's press. They decide who's famous. A good photo from the Flash Mob and you're on every screen in the dungeon. A bad one and you're a joke forever.
You need them on your side to get booked. They know it. They'll make you beg for it.
Strengths: blinding flashes, a crush of bodies and they spit out scandals that drain your fans. Weaknesses: darkness. No light, no pictures.
Break up the Flash Mob and fifty men fall apart and scatter, and some of them will still try and get a photo of you on their way down.

autograph_hound.title: AUTOGRAPH HOUND
lines: Autograph Hounds. People on all fours, sniffing the corridors of the Green Room, with notebooks in their mouths and pens behind their ears, howling for signatures.

They want your autograph. They want everyone's autograph. They'll take it on paper, on skin, on bone. Some of them have the signatures of every star on the Network tattooed across their bodies, and they're always looking for space for a new one.
They're fans. That's the horrible thing. They love you. They'll love you to death. They've loved people to death before.
Strengths: they're fast, they swarm and once one's got your scent, they never stop following. Weaknesses: sign the book. They lose all interest.
Sign something for one and he'll whimper with joy and run away. Then he'll be back tomorrow with forty friends.

agent_twelve_percent.title: AGENT TWELVE PERCENT
agent_twelve_percent.sub: Boss of the Agency. Takes twelve percent of everything.
lines: Agent Twelve Percent. A short, round man in a shiny suit, with slicked-back hair, a phone in each hand, a cigar the size of a rolling pin and a smile that stops a long way from his eyes.

He represents everyone who's anyone in the Green Room. Nobody gets booked without him. He takes twelve percent. Of fees. Of fans. Of your organs, if it comes to it. He has a fridge in his office. Do not open the fridge.
He's never lost a client. He's never had a client who left. He has a filing cabinet full of contracts, and some of the people in them have been dead for seasons and are still paying commission.
Strengths: he summons hounds and paparazzi, he negotiates you into a worse position mid-fight and his contracts bind. Weaknesses: he can't fight. At all. He's a talker.
Sign with him and you'll get booked. Or take his contacts book and get booked anyway, and save yourself twelve percent of a kidney.

jolly_jack_brightly.title: JOLLY JACK BRIGHTLY
jolly_jack_brightly.sub: Boss of the Talk Show. Tonight's host.
lines: Jolly Jack Brightly. A talk-show host with teeth like a piano, hair like a helmet and a suit like a disco ball, beaming from behind a desk, with a mug that says 'WORLD'S BEST HOST' and a couch for his guests that has a trapdoor under it.
He's been hosting the same talk show every night for thirty years. His guests come on, sit on the couch, laugh at his jokes, and, if he doesn't like them, go through the trapdoor into the dark.
He's charming. He's funny. He'll ask you about your childhood and look like he cares. Then he'll tell your worst secret to forty million people and laugh as he does it.
Strengths: interview questions that hurt more than punches, a studio audience that cheers him on and a trapdoor under every seat. Weaknesses: he can't stand being upstaged.
Survive the interview. Then check under the couch. The trapdoor goes somewhere he doesn't want you to know about.

the_producer.title: THE PRODUCER
the_producer.sub: Floor Boss of the Producers' Floor. Wants you to stay.
lines: The Producer. A tall man in an immaculate grey suit, no tie, a glass of something expensive in his hand and an office at the top of the Green Room with a view over the whole studio complex. He's never raised his voice. He's never had to.
He makes the show. Not the episodes, not the scripts: the show. Everything the Network broadcasts comes through his office. He decides who's a star, who's a guest and who's a recurring character.

And he wants you to be a recurring character. Steady work. A dressing room. Your name on the door. Forever. You'd never have to go deeper. You'd never have to see what's down there. That's the offer, and it's the best offer anyone's going to make you.
Strengths: contracts that bind, security that floods the room and the ability to cancel your abilities mid-fight. Weaknesses: refusal. He's never been told no.
Refuse the contract. Watch the smile slip, just for a second. Then he'll say, very quietly, 'Pity,' and press a button under his desk.
